Updated observational data through the afternoon represent the final inputs likely to refine these trader-assessed odds.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Météo France guidance for August 9 points to a maximum of 33°C in Paris under largely sunny skies with light variable winds, establishing the primary driver behind the market’s tight clustering around 33–34°C. Multiple numerical weather prediction models converge on this range, reflecting stable high pressure, southerly flow advecting warmer continental air, and strong daytime insolation without significant cloud cover or precipitation to moderate temperatures. Recent model runs show limited spread, with only modest upside risk to 35°C if boundary-layer mixing proves shallower than expected. Historical August maxima in Paris average near 25°C, so current guidance represents a notable but not extreme warm anomaly consistent with the broader 2026 summer pattern of recurrent heat episodes. Updated Météo France briefings and ensemble outputs tomorrow morning remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift implied probabilities within the narrow 32–35°C window.

title: Highest temperature in Seoul (Incheon) on August 9?

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Korea Meteorological Administration and Incheon International Airport station point to a daytime maximum near 33–34°C on August 9, 2026, under persistent high-pressure conditions and light easterly flow that limit cloud cover and mixing. This aligns with the market’s leading 34°C outcome at 47.5% implied probability, followed closely by 33°C and 35°C. The broader August heatwave, which produced Seoul-area peaks of 37.9–39.9°C earlier in the week, is expected to ease slightly by the 9th as the ridge weakens and onshore flow increases modestly, keeping the distribution centered on 33–35°C bins while still carrying heatwave warnings. Official resolution will use verified Incheon station observations, with model consensus favoring limited further intensification.

**Recent numerical weather prediction model consensus positions Moscow’s maximum temperature on August 9, 2026, most likely between 22 °C and 23 °C.** Multiple sources, including extended-range guidance from AccuWeather, climate-data.org, and weather25.com, converge on a daytime high of 22–23 °C under partly cloudy to broken-cloud conditions with light winds and minimal precipitation. This aligns directly with the market-implied probabilities (22 °C at 46 %, 23 °C at 35.5 %), which represent trader aggregation of short-range model runs and official guidance from Roshydromet.

**Atmospheric steering patterns and typical early-August climatology underpin the narrow distribution.** Moscow’s August mean high is approximately 21–22 °C; the current forecast sits slightly above this baseline but within normal interannual variability. Ensemble spreads from global models remain modest, with only low-probability tails extending to 21 °C or 24 °C, consistent with the 13.5 % and 4.5 % market shares. No significant warm or cold advection signals or blocking patterns have emerged in the past 48 hours to shift the consensus.

**The primary near-term catalyst remains the next model update cycle.** Traders monitor 00Z and 12Z runs from ECMWF, GFS, and regional limited-area models for any adjustment in boundary-layer temperatures or cloud cover. Resolution will use the official daily maximum recorded at Moscow’s Vnukovo or Domodedovo stations, emphasizing the importance of precise local observations over broader regional averages.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus for Shenzhen's August 10 peak temperature centers on 35–36°C (combined ~67% implied probability), reflecting model consensus for a typical late-summer subtropical day tempered by possible cloud cover or scattered showers.**

Shenzhen, located in Guangdong province, experiences August conditions dominated by the East Asian monsoon, with high humidity (often 75–85%), weak steering winds, and frequent afternoon convection. Official and international models (including those referenced in recent forecasts) project daytime maxima of 33–36°C under partly cloudy skies, consistent with August climatology of ~32–33°C average highs. The narrow spread between 35°C and 36°C outcomes stems from uncertainty in boundary-layer moisture and shortwave radiation: clearer intervals or stronger urban heat-island effects in the densely built Pearl River Delta could push readings to 36°C, while increased cloudiness or distant influences from Typhoon Dolphin (tracking toward Zhejiang/Fujian) may cap temperatures near 35°C through enhanced rain-cooled downdrafts.

Recent developments include stable warm, moist southerly flow and no strong cold-air intrusion, keeping probabilities clustered in the mid-30s rather than extreme values. Upcoming model runs and local meteorological briefings over the next 48 hours will likely refine the outcome as the precise timing of any convective activity becomes clearer.
